methods.fixtures: tools/spike_m2_fixtures.ts, seed 20261108: synthetic harmonic tone, 5.5 Hz vibrato, note changes, unvoiced gaps with noise; stereo right channel differs (harmonic weights, gain, noise, 0.4 ms delay). Encoder per file in runs[].encoder.
methods.fileInput: Playwright setInputFiles on <input type=file>, then File.arrayBuffer() in the page.
methods.decode: decodeAudioData on an OfflineAudioContext(1, 1, 48000). decodeMs = decodeAudioData call only; readMs = File.arrayBuffer().
methods.transfer: AudioBuffer.getChannelData arrays posted to a module Worker as transferables (copy fallback reported in result.transferMode).
methods.mix: In the Worker: arithmetic mean of all channels per sample into a Float64Array (as tools/wav.ts). Timed separately as worker.mixMs.
methods.analysis: In the Worker: new FrameAnalyzer({ sampleRate }).run(mono, true) then decodeAll(frames, { lag: Infinity }), the cont path of tools/run_ts.ts. analysisMs = run + decodeAll (same span run_ts.ts times). realTimeFactor = audio seconds / analysis seconds.
methods.retained: After analysis the Worker keeps the mono mix, frames and decoded path alive until the tail of sampling ends, as a result screen would.
methods.memory: ps RSS of the launched Chrome process tree (descendants of the launchServer PID), sampled at about 50 ms (start to start; slower when ps itself takes longer, see memory.meanSampleIntervalMs). Baseline = mean over 1500 ms with the page loaded and the Worker started, after a 2500 ms settle, before the file is set. Peak over the run plus 750 ms tail. Renderer = the renderer process with the highest peak (hosts the page and its Worker).
memoryCaveats: RSS is resident pages only. On macOS, memory that is compressed or swapped is not in RSS, and shared pages are counted in every process that maps them, so the tree sum can double-count shared memory. Activity Monitor shows phys_footprint, which can differ.
Sampling at about 50 ms (see meanSampleIntervalMs and maxSampleIntervalMs per run) can miss short spikes between samples.
Garbage collection timing changes the peak: freed buffers may stay resident until the next GC.
Headless Chrome on an otherwise busy machine; a headed tab adds compositor and GPU memory not measured here.
One run per file; timings were not repeated, so run-to-run variance is unknown.
